title: A proper projective-space map with embedded fibre is finite near that base point
statement: Let $S$ and $Z$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $r\geq0$, put $P=\mathbf P^r_S$ with projection $q:P\to S$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], and let $\varphi:Z\to P$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Set $f=q\circ\varphi$ and fix $s\in S$. Assume the base-changed morphism $\varphi_s:Z_s\to\mathbf P^r_{\kappa(s)}$, where fibres are scheme-theoretic [def-pc-scheme-fibre], is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. There is an affine open neighbourhood $V\subseteq S$ of $s$ such that the restriction $\varphi_V:f^{-1}(V)\to q^{-1}(V)=\mathbf P^r_V$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. No Noetherian hypothesis on $S$, nonemptiness of the fibre, or surjectivity of $\varphi_s$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0D2N, lemma-ample-in-neighbourhood, final paragraph: finite over a neighbourhood of the entire projective-space fibre, then shrink the base using closedness of projective space.

proof.text: Fix $p\in q^{-1}(s)$. By [def-pc-scheme-fibre], the fibre projections identify $|Z_s|$ with $f^{-1}(s)$ and $|P_s|$ with $q^{-1}(s)$. The induced map $\varphi_s$ commutes with these projections by the defining fibre-product equations. Its underlying map is injective by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. If $z_1,z_2\in\varphi^{-1}(p)$, then $f(z_i)=q(p)=s$; their unique lifts to $Z_s$ therefore have equal images in $P_s$, hence are equal. Thus $z_1=z_2$, and $\varphi^{-1}(p)$ has at most one point, including when it is empty.

source.place: Tag 0D2N, final paragraph; explicit point-set consequence of the embedded fibre

proof.text: For every $p\in q^{-1}(s)$ apply [lem-trf-proper-finite-fibre-finite-near] to the proper morphism $\varphi:Z\to P$ and its finite underlying fibre at $p$. Obtain an open $W_p\subseteq P$ containing $p$ on which $\varphi$ is finite. Put $W=\bigcup_{p\in q^{-1}(s)}W_p$. These opens cover $W$, and the restrictions of $\varphi^{-1}(W)\to W$ over them are exactly the finite maps just obtained. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-local-on-target], condition (3), makes $\varphi^{-1}(W)\to W$ finite. In particular $q^{-1}(s)\subseteq W$.

source.place: Tag 0D2N, final paragraph, finite over an open neighbourhood of the entire projective fibre; arbitrary-base input is Tag 02UP in more-morphisms.tex, lemma-proper-finite-fibre-finite-in-neighbourhood

proof.text: Take the coordinate index set $\{0,\ldots,r\}$. By [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], $q:P\to S$ is proper, and therefore is closed by [def-weil-proper-morphism] (use the identity base change). Thus $C=q(P\setminus W)$ is closed. Since the whole fibre $q^{-1}(s)$ lies in $W$, $s\notin C$. Set $V_0=S\setminus C$. Then $s\in V_0$ and $q^{-1}(V_0)\subseteq W$: otherwise a point outside $W$ would map both into $C$ and into $V_0$.

source.place: Tag 0D2N, final paragraph, use closedness of projective space to shrink the base

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], choose an affine open $s\in V\subseteq V_0$. Then $q^{-1}(V)$ is an open subscheme of $W$. Apply the restriction clause of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-local-on-target] to the finite map $\varphi^{-1}(W)\to W$: its restriction over $q^{-1}(V)$ is finite. Its source is $\varphi^{-1}(q^{-1}(V))=f^{-1}(V)$, so this is exactly the required $\varphi_V$.
